item.title: Jury Deliberations Underway in Lindsay Clancy Murder Trial
item.description: In order to reach a verdict, jurors must agree on whether Ms. Clancy should be held criminally responsible for killing her three children.
item.dc:creator: Jacey Fortin
item.media:description: Jury deliberations are set to resume on Friday in the trial of Lindsay Clancy.

item.title: Wyoming Governor Objects to ‘Very Odd’ D.O.J. Election Monitoring
item.description: Governor Mark Gordon, a Republican, said he was concerned by the behavior of election observers who visited a polling station in Cheyenne.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:credit: Haiyun Jiang for The New York Times
item.media:description: Governor Mark Gordon of Wyoming leads one of the most conservative states.

item.title: With Term Winding Down, Pelosi Tries to Anoint a Successor
item.description: Representative Nancy Pelosi, the former House speaker, has been working hard on behalf of Connie Chan, a San Francisco supervisor with a relatively low profile in California.
item.dc:creator: Heather Knight
item.media:description: Representative Nancy Pelosi has endorsed Connie Chan, a San Francisco supervisor, in the race for her congressional seat.

item.title: The Town Council Race Was Tied. The Three of Spades Called It.
item.description: Two candidates for Town Council in Gila Bend, Ariz., finished with the same number of votes. A century-old state law mandated breaking the tie with a game of chance.
item.dc:creator: Reis Thebault
item.media:credit: Anna Watts for The New York Times
item.media:description: Patricia Riggs, the interim town clerk of Gila Bend, Ariz., declared Jesus Rubalcava the winner of the Town Council seat after a game of high-card draw with the opposing candidate, Athena Guerrero.

item.title: How Key Oil Stockpiles Dwindled During the War in Iran
item.description: Our energy reporter Rebecca F. Elliott explains how oil reserves helped prevent an oil shock caused by the war in Iran from getting even worse — and how low those reserves are now.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca F. Elliott, Paul Abowd, Jon Miller, Edward Vega, Rafaela Balster, June Kim and Leanne Abraham
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)

item.title: Judge Once Again Bars Postal Service From Restricting Mail-In Vote
item.description: After reviewing the agency’s final plan to comply with President Trump’s demands, a federal judge barred the Postal Service from imposing new restrictions on mail-in voting.
item.dc:creator: Zach Montague
item.media:credit: Zack Wittman for The New York Times
item.media:description: In a filing on Thursday, the Postal Service denied that its proposal left any room for it to second-guess states on which voters were eligible to cast a ballot.

item.title: LA Mayor Karen Bass Eases Street Vending Crackdown After Debate
item.description: Mayor Karen Bass said food vendors discourage restaurant patrons, mentioning them alongside homeless encampments. Her opponent, Nithya Raman, said vendors should be brought into the system.
item.dc:creator: Livia Albeck-Ripka
item.media:credit: Ariana Drehsler for The New York Times
item.media:description: Street vendors are ubiquitous presences across the Los Angeles area, offering foods from many cultures.

item.title: Lake Ontario Didn’t Ask for Trump to Rename It

item.dc:creator: Katie Rogers
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Boats were anchored along the waterfront of Lake Ontario in Toronto on Thursday.

item.title: ‘I Need to Go to the Hospital,’ Delta Pilot Tells Air Traffic Control

item.title: Climber Stranded for Hours on 6-Inch Rock Ledge Before Rescue
item.description: Racing against the darkness, rescuers in California on Saturday saved a man who had become stranded on a ledge perched atop a soaring peak on the Sierra Nevada.

item.title: Trump Plans to Mark 9/11 at the Pentagon, Not Ground Zero
item.description: President Trump originally intended to commemorate the 25th anniversary of Sept. 11 with remarks at ground zero, but the memorial’s organizers do not allow speeches. Mr. Trump changed his plans.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Haberman, Zolan Kanno-Youngs, Dana Rubinstein and Sally Goldenberg
item.media:description: Memorials left at the south tower reflecting pool last year at the World Trade Center in Manhattan.

item.title: Man Flees Fire at His Home in Stolen Rescue Truck, Police Say
item.description: Officials in New Hampshire said the man used the rescue truck as a weapon, nearly striking emergency responders who were trying to save his rural house.

item.title: Trump Administration Will Appeal Harvard Antisemitism Case

item.dc:creator: Alan Blinder
item.media:credit: Lucy Lu for The New York Times
item.media:description: A legal conflict between the Trump administration and Harvard has lasted for over a year.

item.title: White House Construction May Have Contributed to Close Call With Trump’s Helicopter
item.description: A controller let a jet take off after missing warnings that Marine One was about to fly through the area, according to the National Transportation Safety Board.
item.dc:creator: Karoun Demirjian
item.media:credit: Kent Nishimura for The New York Times
item.media:description: A passenger jet came within a mile of Marine One in early August, after an air traffic controller at Ronald Reagan National Airport appeared to have missed multiple warnings.

item.title: Progressives Condemn Pick of Pro-Israel Democrat Atop House Panel
item.description: Outrage over making Representative Jared Moskowitz, who is vocally pro-Israel, the top Democrat on a Middle East policy subcommittee reflected the party’s rift over Israel.
item.dc:creator: Annie Karni
item.media:description: On Tuesday, Representative Jared Moskowitz of Florida, a vocally pro-Israel Democrat, was chosen to serve as the ranking member on a key subcommittee with jurisdiction over Middle East policy.

item.title: Kansas Judge Dismisses Murder Charge Against Sheriff’s Deputy

item.title: Fired Journalists From Stars and Stripes Sue Pentagon

item.title: In Trump’s Washington, Ballooning National Debt Stirs Little Action
